Blanco Trading Post, or 23 miles southeast of Bloomfield, moving

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 24 at 1:01PM MDT until October 24 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...
East Central McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 101 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Laguna Pueblo, Skyline-Ganipa, Acoma Pueblo, San Fidel, Cubero,
McCartys, New Laguna, Cebolletita and San Mateo.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 92 and 114.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Find an
alternate route.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 5:00 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 5:00 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache, Central Mineral and Western Rio
Grande Counties...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1234 PM MDT, Gauge reports indicate high water levels in area
creeks and streams continuing, although many locations in the San
Juan Mountains have crested and have begun to slowly fall. Over
the western portion of the San Luis Valley, many streams and
creeks are near crest now and will slowly fall for the remainder
of the day. The Conejos River at Mogote has crested, but will
likely remain above flood stage until early Monday morning.
- Please heed all road closures and evacuation or shelter in place
orders.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Cumbres Pass, Platoro, Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves up to 6 feet in the surf zone. For the
High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal New Hanover County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Monday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
